blocks.content:
The Constitution ensures judicial independence through:
• Security of tenure
• Fixed service conditions
• Salaries charged on Consolidated Fund of India
• Separation from executive
• Difficult removal procedure
The Constitution ensures judicial independence through:

items: Judicial salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, meaning they are non-votable by Parliament.
Separation of the judiciary from the executive is a constitutional provision frequently asked in Polity prelims.
The complex removal procedure of judges safeguards security of tenure against executive overreach.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Judges enjoy security of tenure to function without fear or favor.
Service conditions of judges are fixed to prevent arbitrary modifications.
Salaries and allowances are charged directly on the Consolidated Fund of India.
The Constitution mandates the separation of the judiciary from the executive.
A difficult removal procedure ensures immunity from political interference.
